* Duration cards remain in play until the Clean-up phase of the last turn on which they are expected to have an effect; Throne Room variants playing Duration cards remain in play until the Clean-up phase of the turn when the Duration leaves play.
* One-shots, Reserve cards, and certain other cards have instructions to remove themselves from play as a result of playing them.
* Some cards and card-shaped things have abilities that cause you to remove other cards from play before the Clean-up phase, or do something else with them in the Clean-up phase instead of discarding them: for example, {card:Crypt} sets aside Treasure cards from play when you play it, and {card:Improve} trashes a card from play during Clean-up instead of discarding it.
* {card:Royal Galley} and {card:Journey} instruct you to leave cards in play that would ordinarily be discarded.

Note that cards on mats or that are set aside are not in play. For example the card set aside by {card:Blockade} is not in play although Blockade itself is. Landscapes, such as Artifacts, are also never in play, even if moved to your play area, as they are not "played".

Some cards and card-shaped things have abilities that depend on what is in play at a given time. For example, {card:Peddler} changes its own cost depending on how many Action cards are in play during the Buy phase, and {card:Changeling} can only gain copies of cards that are in play.

sections.heading: Being played vs. in play
sections.body:
Due to the existence of Throne Room variants, one-shots, Command variants, Reserve cards, and Duration cards, being in play and being played are different conditions that can have different consequences. Confusion resulting from this was a major factor in the elimination of while-in-play card abilities (see below), but some potential for confusion still remains, since some cards have abilities that depend on what cards are in play, while other cards have abilities that depend on what cards have been played. For example, {card:Fool's Gold}'s ability depends on how many times Fool's Gold *has been played* in a given turn (so for example, playing the same Fool's Gold twice with {card:Crown} can give different results), while {card:Idol} and {card:Aristocrat} have abilities that depend on how many copies of them are in play (so playing the same copy of the card twice in a row won't give different effects). Similarly, {card:Conspirator}'s cantrip effect depends on how many other Action cards have been played on the turn, regardless of whether they are still in play, while {card:Peddler}'s cost reduction depends on how many Action cards are in play, regardless of how many have been played.

Note that Reactions are neither in play nor played unless the explicitly instruct you to play them. For example, {card:Clerk} and {card:Trail} are played when using their reactions, but revealing {card:Moat} or {card:Watchtower} does not play them.

sections.heading: While-in-play abilities
sections.body:
Between Seaside in 2009 and Nocturne in 2017, a number of Dominion cards were released with abilities that are activated **while the card is in play**, listed below a horizontal dividing line in the card text; these may be contrasted with "on-play" (or "above-the-line") abilities, which are triggered by the card *being played*, rather than by it being *located in the play area*. Cards with while-in-play abilities were typically those with persistent effects on the game state that lasted for a period of time; Donald X. Vaccarino's rationale in introducing the while-in-play mechanic was to facilitate tracking of these abilities, so players could simply inspect the cards that were visible in the play area to determine which abilities were in effect.

However, players often found the rules for while-in-play abilities, and the differences between them and on-play abilities, confusing and counterintuitive—especially in cases where the same ability (such as cost reduction) was on-play for some cards (e.g., {card:Bridge}) and while-in-play for others (e.g., {card:Highway}). As a result of this confusion, Donald X. eventually stopped introducing while-in-play abilities on new cards; and in the 2022 updates and revisions, all remaining cards with while-in-play abilities either were removed to be replaced with new cards in the second edition of Prosperity, or were revised to move the abilities above the line.

sections.heading: Differences between while-in-play and on-play
sections.body:
Since while-in-play abilities begin to take effect when you play the card, it is easy to mistake them for abilities that are triggered *by* playing the card. However, while-in-play effects differ from on-play effects in several ways:
* If you play the same card multiple times on the same turn via a Throne Room variant, its "on-play" abilities happen each time you play it; but there is only one copy of the card in the play area, so its while-in-play abilities only happen once.
* If a card is played by a Command variant, it never enters play, so its while-in-play abilities never activate but its on-play effects do. Similarly, if a card is removed from play prematurely, its while-in-play abilities cease to operate, but any persistent on-play abilities remain in effect.
* {card:Enchantress} and Ways overrule the on-play abilities of an Action card, but leave the while-in-play abilities unchanged; {card:Highwayman} and {card:Enlightenment} do the same for a Treasure card.

sections.heading: List of cards with while-in-play abilities
Related abilities
sections.body:
No "while-in-play" abilities representing persistent effects remain. However, several cards still have below-the-line abilities that depend on the card being in play at a given time, or activate when the card is being discarded from play. These abilities are still subject to the rules differences noted above—in particular, when the following cards are played using a Way, or subject to the effect of {card:Enchantress}, {card:Enlightenment}, or {card:Highwayman}, their below-the-line abilities are still in force.

* {card:Capital} — When discarded from play, {debt:+6}.
* {card:Merchant Camp} — When discarded from play, you may put it onto your deck.
* {card:Tent} — When discarded from play, you may put it onto your deck.
* {card:Urchin} — When playing another Attack card, you may trash Urchin from play to gain a {card:Madman}.
* {card:Walled Village} — At the start of Clean-up, you may put it onto your deck if you have no more than one other card in play.
* All Travellers — When discarded from play, you may exchange it for the next card in its Traveller line.

The effects of the Traits {card:Reckless} and {card:Tireless}, the Artifact {card:Horn}, and the Prophecy {card:Panic} that move a card when it is discarded from play are not strictly speaking "below the line", but they are similarly not overruled by Ways, {card:Enchantress}, or {card:Highwayman}.

sections.heading: Donald X.'s evolving thoughts on while-in-play
sections.body:
Donald X. originally introduced while-in-play abilities for the sake of tracking persistent effects:

At one point he contemplated revising earlier cards such as {card:Bridge} to use while-in-play wording, though he did not end up making this change.

Later, he discovered that players find while-in-play abilities more confusing than on-play abilities, and stopped using while-in-play abilities on new cards:

Finally, in 2022, all cards with "while this is in play" received errata to "this turn."

__FORCETOC__

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body:
, a Trait.]]

**Traits**, introduced in Plunder, are effects that modify default behavior of a Kingdom pile they are attached to.

Traits are not Kingdom cards.

There are 15 Traits, any number of which may be used in a game of Dominion, though Donald X. recommends not using more than two total Landmarks, Events, Projects, Ways, and Traits. When choosing a random Kingdom, the Traits may be shuffled into the randomizer deck; any Traits that are dealt once 10 Kingdom cards have also been dealt will be included in the game.
At the start of a game with a Trait, you randomly pick which eligible pile (only Action and Treasure piles) is modified, and the Trait card can slide under the pile, leaving the text showing and the name on the sides. Hence the layout.

sections.heading: Official rules
sections.body:
Plunder has Traits, which are a new kind of landscape card that affects a single Action or Treasure pile. At the start of a game with a Trait, choose a random Action or Treasure Kingdom card pile to put the Trait on; then during that game, cards from that pile are affected as indicated on the Trait.
<onlyinclude>* Traits are not Kingdom cards, and are never bought or gained.
* Traits only go on Kingdom cards, not on e.g. {card:Silver} or the Ruins pile (from Dark Ages).
* Don't put two Traits on the same pile.
* Traits refer to the pile using the name of the Trait; for example {card:Pious} refers to "Pious cards." That just means, any card from that pile.
* A Trait on a split pile (from Empires and Allies) affects all of those different cards.
* Traits continue to affect the cards from a pile even after the pile is empty.</onlyinclude>

sections.heading: Preparation
sections.body:
* Events and Traits can be shuffled into the randomizer deck (despite having a different back). They are not part of the 10 Kingdom cards used in a game; when an Event or Trait is turned over, put it on the table but keep turning over cards until you get 10 Kingdom cards. For normal play we recommend using at most 2 such cards; with other expansions that includes Events, Traits, Landmarks, Projects, and Ways. Skip any further landscape cards turned over. Also skip Events and Traits when using a randomizer card to determine whether or not to use {card:Platinum}/{card:Colony} (from Prosperity), or Shelters (from Dark Ages) in a game, or to determine the bane for {card:Young Witch} (from Cornucopia). Another approach some people may prefer is to shuffle Events and Traits (and Landmarks, Projects, and Ways) separately into their own deck, and always play with one or two of them.
* In games using a Trait, pick a random Treasure or Action from the dealt-out Kingdom cards and put the Trait under it, so the text is showing; do not put two Traits on the same pile.

sections.heading: Other rules clarifications
sections.body:
* The Trait is not a type, e.g. revealing a card affected by a Trait will not give you an extra choice from {card:Courtier}.
* If {card:Divine Wind} goes into effect, the pile with the Trait is removed from the supply, but cards from that removed pile still have the Trait.

sections.heading: List of Traits
sections.body: {card:Cheap}, {card:Cursed}, {card:Fated}, {card:Fawning}, {card:Friendly}, {card:Hasty}, {card:Inherited}, {card:Inspiring}, {card:Nearby}, {card:Patient}, {card:Pious}, {card:Reckless}, {card:Rich}, {card:Shy}, {card:Tireless}

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body:
The **2016 Errata** adjusts the wordings and formatting of all cards in the pre-Empires sets. Only a few cards received changed that actually affected how they are played while many more were reworded to have clearer meaning or just to need less text.

This was the first Errata and coincided with the Second Editions of Base and Intrigue.

Changes to card layout were first announced in May 2016, a few days before Empires was previewed. The changes were visible in reprints during 2016 to 2018.

sections.heading: Shuffling rule
sections.body:
Previously, when you wanted to draw a card (or otherwise do something with your deck), and your deck was empty, you shuffled, then continued drawing. So if you played {card:Smithy} with 2 cards left in your deck, you would have drawn those 2, then shuffled, and drawn 1 more. With the new rule, when your deck is running low, you first check to see if there's enough left to do something with, and if there's not, you shuffle your discard pile, and put that under what's left of your deck. So in the aforementioned situation, with 2 cards left in your deck when you play Smithy, you'd shuffle your discard pile, slide it under those 2 cards, and then draw your 3 cards. Donald X. has cited the ruling as making it easier for situations other than drawing with a near-empty deck.

This has no functional effect on gameplay, except for when {card:Stash}, which is therefore updated to let you look at what remains of your deck when you shuffle, in order to retain its function despite the new rule.

sections.heading: Functional card changes
sections.body:
* {card:Cellar}, *{card:Oracle}*, {card:Storeroom}, {card:Storyteller} — Rephrased to use "draw X cards" instead of "+X Cards". (This was later reverted by the 2020 Errata.)
* {card:Borrow}, {card:Save} — Only give +Buy once per turn.
* *{card:Embargo}* — Each {card:Curse} gained per token on a pile is a separate event, rather than gaining all of them at once.
* {card:Masquerade} — Players with no cards in hand are skipped.
* {card:Mine}, {card:Moneylender}, {card:Throne Room} — Trashing/Playing a card is now optional, for accountability purposes.
* {card:Outpost} — Changed to function in a similar way to {card:Mission}.
* *{card:Pirate Ship}* — Reordered options to have gaining {cost:} before attacking. (This matters if played with {card:Elder}.)
* {card:Possession} — The Possessing player also receives all {debt:} tokens (from Empires) gained.
* {card:Scheme} — Top-decks an Action card when it is discarded rather than at the start of the Clean-up phase.
* {card:Soothsayer} — Each player both gains a Curse and draws a card before the next player does so, which could matter with some combination of Reactions being used.
* *{card:Trade Route}* — Trash before gaining {cost:}, which matters if trashing a card that can gain Victory cards when trashed (such as {card:Hunting Grounds}).

sections.heading: Coffers
sections.body: The name Coffers was introduced to refer to the Coin tokens from Guilds and all references to "take X Coin tokens" were changed to "+**X Coffers**". This has no effect on any actual gameplay, but does let the text on the relevant cards ({card:Baker}, {card:Butcher}, {card:Candlestick Maker}, {card:Merchant Guild}, {card:Plaza}) take up a little less space, and highlights the taking of Coffers by making it a vanilla bonus. This also helps to distinguish coin tokens used for this purpose from the tokens used by *{card:Pirate Ship}* and *{card:Trade Route}*. Future (re)prints of expansions using Coffers also come with a Coffers mat to further help keeping the tokens apart.

sections.heading: New artwork
sections.body:
* The basic cards ({card:Copper}, {card:Silver}, {card:Gold}, {card:Potion}, {card:Platinum}, {card:Curse}, {card:Estate}, {card:Duchy}, {card:Province}, and {card:Colony}) were updated to use the same artwork as in the Base Cards set.
* The Base Cards set now has its own icon .
* All Promo cards now have the same icon instead of having individual icons. The existing promos that were updated due to this were {card:Black Market}, {card:Envoy}, {card:Governor}, {card:Prince}, {card:Stash}, and {card:Walled Village}.
* The colors on {card:Hovel} and {card:Overgrown Estate} where swapped so Shelter red is now below the Reaction blue and Victory green.

sections.heading: Older changes
sections.body:
Some changes were already visible on cards from the newer expansions before 2016, meaning these were in reality errata from 2010 to 2015 that were now being applied retroactively to the earlier sets too.

* Shorten "trash this card" to "trash this". (Old phrasing was not used in Seaside and later expansions except for Embargo and the Knights.)
** *{card:Embargo}*, {card:Mining Village}, all Knights (*{card:Feast}* also used this phrasing but was removed and was not updated to change it.)
* Only use the name when referring to specific cards, for example "Curse" instead of "Curse card". (The old phrasing was not used in Alchemy and later expansions except for a single card each in Prosperity and Cornucopia.)
** {card:Bureaucrat}, *{card:Counting House}*, {card:Cutpurse}, *{card:Fortune Teller}*, {card:Golem}, {card:Torturer}, {card:Treasure Map}, {card:Witch}
* Shorten "rounded down" to "round down". (The old phrasing was not used in Hinterlands and later expansions.)
** {card:Bishop}, {card:Gardens}, {card:Philosopher's Stone}, {card:Vineyard} (Vineyard was changed back to "rounded down" in 2021.)
* Use "and" instead of comma when listing vanilla bonuses in text, for example "+1 Card and +1 Action" instead of "+1 Card, +1 Action". (The old phrasing was not used in Hinterlands and later expansions except for a single card in Empires.)
** {card:Conspirator}, {card:Fishing Village}, {card:Sacrifice}, *{card:Tournament}*, {card:Wharf}
* Use "play an Action card from you hand X times" instead of "choose an Action card in you hand. Play it X times". (The old phrasing was not used in Dark Ages and later expansions.)
** {card:Throne Room}, {card:King's Court}
* Prefer "Do X to Y" or "Do X for Y" instead of "Do X. If you do, Y." (The old phrasing was not used in Adventures.)
** {card:Baron}, {card:Beggar}, {card:Hamlet}, {card:Market Square}, {card:Mining Village}, {card:Moat}, {card:Moneylender}, {card:Plaza}, {card:Spice Merchant}, {card:Stables}, {card:Trader}, {card:Tunnel}, {card:Urchin}, {card:Vault}, {card:Watchtower}
* Shorten "the trashed card" to "it". (The old phrasing was not used in Adventures.)
** {card:Expand}, {card:Farmland}, {card:Remake}, {card:Remodel}, *{card:Taxman}*
* Shorten "card that is not a Treasure" to "non-Treasure". (The old phrasing was not used in Adventures.)
** {card:Haggler}, {card:Hermit}, {card:Jack of All Trades}, *{card:Talisman}* (However {card:Golem} was not changed to say "non-Golem".)

sections.heading: Clarifications
sections.body:
These cards were reworder specifically to make their meaning less ambiguous.

* {card:Armory}, {card:Artificer}, *{card:Bag of Gold}*, {card:Beggar}, {card:Bureaucrat}, {card:Develop}, *{card:Explorer}*, {card:Fool's Gold}, *{card:Ill-Gotten Gains}*, {card:Mine}, {card:Rocks}, *{card:Sea Hag}*, *{card:Taxman}*, *{card:Tournament}*, {card:Trading Post}, {card:Transmogrify}, {card:Treasure Map} — Replace "gain X, putting it on top of your deck" and "gain X, putting it into your hand" with "gain X onto your deck" and "gain X to your hand" to make it clear that the gained card doesn't visit the discard pile.
* {card:Beggar}, {card:Caravan Guard}, {card:Moat}, *{card:Horse Traders}*, {card:Urchin} — Clarify that reaction happens "first" when an the Attack card is played.
* {card:Black Market} — Explicitly state that the player may play Treasures before buying a card from the Black Market deck.
* {card:Coin of the Realm}, {card:Royal Carriage} — Now refer to finishing "playing" an Action, as opposed to "resolving", which had never been referenced on any other card. (This was revised again in 2021 to become "After you play an Action card".)
* {card:Envoy} — Now says "put in hand" rather than "draw", matching its intended function to ignore the -1 Card token.
* {card:Gardens}, {card:Fairgrounds}, {card:Feodum}, *{card:Silk Road}*, {card:Vineyard} — Change "X in your deck" to "X you have" to make it clearer that all cards count, even if set-aside or on mats.
* {card:Gear}, {card:Haven} — Specify that the set-aside card goes under this card.
* {card:Ironworks} — Explicitly state "the gained card" to make it clearer that "it" wasn't refering to a would-be gained or other card.
* {card:Lookout} — Clarify that the third card goes back on top of the deck.
* *{card:Nomad Camp}* — Rephrased to make it clear it doesn't visit the discard pile, as previously its wording matched {card:Villa|Villa's}, which *does* visit.
* *{card:Pirate Ship}* — Clarify that the coin token goes on the Pirate Ship mat and can't be used as a Coffers.
* {card:Poor House} — Rephrased that the total {cost:} can't go below {cost:0}.
* {card:Giant}, {card:Ranger} — Add a "then" to clarify that state of the Journey token should be checked after turning it over.
* {card:Storyteller} — Clarify that the {coin:+1} from Storyteller is also spent for drawing.
* {card:Torturer} — Clarify that it's allowed to pick an option you can't do.

sections.heading: Other general changes
Additional individual changes
sections.body:
Remaining changes that were specific to each card, generally to make the texts shorter.

* {card:Advisor}, {card:Cartographer}, {card:Farmland}, {card:Forager}, {card:Library}, *{card:Noble Brigand}*, {card:Rebuild}, {card:Tactician}, {card:Wishing Well} — Combine statements (often using "and" or "then") instead of having separate sentences.
* {card:Band of Misfits}, {card:Border Village}, {card:Haggler} — Shorten "costing less than" to "cheaper". (However {card:Stonemason} was not updated and both phrasings are used on cards in later expansions.)
* {card:Beggar}, *{card:Cache}* — Specify multiple number of cards with numbers, i.e. "2" instead of "two". (However the 2022 version of {card:Bonfire} uses "two" instead of "2".)
* {card:Bridge} — Shorten "All cards (including cards in players' hands)" to "This turn, cards (everywhere)".
* *{card:Duchess}* — Shorten "discards it or puts it back" to "may discard it".
* {card:Fool's Gold} — Change "If ..., this is worth {cost:1}" to "Worth {cost:1} if ...".
* {card:Grand Market} — Use "Coppers" instead of "Copper" as the plural form.
* {card:Grand Market} — Mark cost with an asterisk.
* {card:Horn of Plenty} — Remove the large {cost:0}. (The upper corners would continue to show the card's value as {cost:0} until 2022.)
* {card:Hunting Party}, {card:Menagerie} — Use "copy" or "different names" instead of "duplicate" when comparing if two cards are the same.
* {card:Inn} — Reword the reminder that the gained Inn can be part of the cards chosen from the discard.
* {card:Island}, {card:Native Village} — Remove the reminders to return set-aside cards to the deck at the end of the game.
* {card:Jack of All Trades} — Now has the word "all" in its name capitalized.
* *{card:Masterpiece}* — Use the same "For each {cost:1} you overpaid" phrasing as the other overpay cards.
* {card:Mission} — Change "in" to "during" when refering to the extra turn.
* {card:Scouting Party} — Remove the redundant "of them".
* {card:Summon} — Change "if you do" to "if you did".
* *{card:Taxman}* — Shorten "or reveals a hand without it" to "or reveals they can't".
* {card:Treasure Map} — Remove the redundant "another copy of".
* *{card:Trusty Steed}* — Add "or" between each option. (In 2024 Trusted Steed was replaced by {card:Courser} which does not use "or".)
* {card:Tunnel} — Shorten "Clean-up phase" to "Clean-up".
* {card:Warrior} — Change "For each Traveller" to "Once per Traveller". (This was later reverted in 2021.)

sections.heading: Formatting changes
sections.body:
(These changes apply to all cards in Adventures and older sets so the list of affected cards are not explicitly listed here.)
* The font size was increased when the amount of text is small enough to allow it.
* **+X Cards**, **+X Buys**, {vp:1}, etc. in the body text were changed to bold.
* The plus in **+X Cards** etc. is now consistently the same style as the text instead of sometimes being a different style.
* Card texts became better centered.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body:
The **2022 Errata** updated cards in all pre-Allies sets to simplify their phrasing and make their rules less confusing.

This was the third large errata and coincided with the Second Edition of Seaside, Prosperity, and Hinterlands.

sections.heading: Clarification whether the Buy phase ends
sections.body: Returning to your Action phase from your Buy phase, e.g. with {card:Villa} or {card:Cavalry}, counts as ending it, and will thus trigger effects that occur at the end of the Buy phase, such as with {card:Wine Merchant}, right then.

sections.heading: Replaced when-buy
sections.body:
The when-buy trigger is removed to avoid confusions with when-gain triggers.
* {card:Charm}, {card:Forum}, {card:Hovel}, {card:Mint}, {card:Plan}, {card:Port} — The condition is simply changed from buying to gaining.
* {card:Basilica}, {card:Colonnade}, {card:Defiled Shrine}, {card:Exploration}, {card:Hermit}, {card:Messenger}, {card:Tax}, {card:Treasury} — The condition is limited to gained during the Buy phase.
** {card:Basilica} and {card:Colonnade} were initially changed to trigger on any gain but was shortly after erratad again to only trigger on gains in the Buy phase.
* {card:Haggler}, {card:Haunted Woods}, {card:Hoard}, {card:Swamp Hag} — Triggers when gaining a card that was bought.
* {card:Farmland} — Triggers on gaining, and can no longer gain a Farmland card.
* {card:Herald}, {card:Stonemason}, *{card:Doctor}*, *{card:Masterpiece}* — Overpay abilities are resolved when the card is gained.
Technically, cards *{card:Embargo}*, *{card:Goons}*, *{card:Noble Brigand}*, *{card:Talisman}* also fall into this category, but these have become removed cards in the interim and remain unchanged.

sections.heading: Replaced "while this is in play"
sections.body:
Cards no longer use the condition "while this is in play" or "while you have this in play".
* {card:Groundskeeper}, {card:Haggler}, {card:Highway}, {card:Hoard}, *{card:Princess}*, {card:Quarry}, {card:Sauna}, {card:Tracker} — Active during this turn.
* {card:Bridge Troll} — Active during this turn and your next turn.
* {card:Lighthouse} — Active until the start of your next turn.
Technically, cards *{card:Goons}*, *{card:Royal Seal}*, and *{card:Talisman}* also fall into this category, but these have become removed cards in the interim and remain unchanged.

sections.heading: Duration tracking
sections.body:
Avoid tracking issues by not moving Durations that are in play.
* {card:Bonfire} — Only trashes {card:Copper|Coppers}.
* {card:Counterfeit}, {card:Mint}, {card:Crypt} — Only trash or set aside non-Duration cards.
Technically, *{card:Mandarin}* also fall in this category but has become removed in the interim and remain unchanged.

sections.heading: Preventing Command card loops
sections.body:
* {card:Inheritance} — Inherited {card:Estate|Estates} also gain the Command type.
* {card:Prince} — No longer allows Command type cards to be set aside.

sections.heading: Other functional card changes
sections.body:
* {card:Alchemist} — Triggers at the start of Clean-up instead of when it's discarded.
* {card:Citadel} — Replays the card afterwards instead of playing the card twice to avoid unintended interactions with cards played by {card:Captain}.
* {card:Donate} — Triggers at the start of your next turn instead of in-between turns.
** The errata was initially to trigger {card:Donate} the same turn before drawing but was shortly after revised again to trigger at the start of next turn.
* {card:Herbalist} — Triggers when a Treasure is discarded instead of when this is discarded.
* {card:Hermit} — Exchanges itself for a {card:Madman} instead of being trashed.
* {card:Hermit}, {card:Treasury} — Triggers at the end of the Buy phase instead of when discarded. (This was later reverted for Treasury by the 2026 Errata.)
* {card:Innovation} — The player can choose any gained Action card to play, not just the first.
* {card:Mountain Pass} — Triggers immediately when a {card:Province} is bought instead of after that turn.
* {card:Prince} — Is now a Duration, can no longer set aside Duration cards, and the set aside card now stays set aside when played, making it a command variant.
* {card:Storyteller} — Gives +1 Card after converting {cost:} to cards instead of {coin:+1} before converting.

sections.heading: Cosmetic card changes
sections.body:
The following changes makes the wordings on cards simpler or more consistent but does not affect how they are played.
* {card:Bridge Troll}, {card:Haunted Woods}, {card:Swamp Hag} — The card types are reordered from Action-Attack-Duration to Action-Duration-Attack.
* {card:Butcher}, {card:Haunted Castle}, and {card:Young Witch} — Rephrased to shorten their texts.
* {card:Caravan Guard} — No longer reminds that +1 Action isn't usable on other player's turns.
* {card:Champion} — Clarify that +1 Action occurs before resolving each Action card.
* {card:Champion}, {card:Hireling} — Removed "this stays in play" reminder on Durations that last multiple turns.
* {card:Counterfeit} — Remove redundant "If you do" and shorten "that Treasure" to "it".
* {card:Guardian}, {card:Haunted Woods}, {card:Swamp Hag} — Prefer "At X do Y. Until then Z" over "Until X do Z. At X do Y.". (However {card:Enchantress} and {card:Monkey} still use the old wording.)
* {card:Inn} — Remove reminder that the gained Inn can be included in the chosen cards.
* {card:Mission} — Added a reminder that Events can be bought during the Mission turn.
* {card:Horn of Plenty} — Don't show the Treasure value as {cost:0} in upper corners for cards that don't produce any {cost:}. ({card:Ducat} and {card:Sunken Treasure} have not been updated but are likely to the next time they are reprinted.)

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: The **2020 Errata** made some smaller changes to pre-Menagerie sets.

sections.heading: Functional card changes
sections.body:
* {card:Bank}, {card:Fool's Gold}, {card:Philosopher's Stone} — Treasures use {coin:+} instead of "worth". (Affects cards caring about {coin:+}, like {card:Way of the Chameleon}.)
* {card:Cellar}, *{card:Oracle}*, {card:Storyteller} — Changed back from "draw" to "+X Cards" (reverting the 2016 Errata). ({card:Storeroom} still use "draw" but it is likely that it too will change in a future reprint of Dark Ages.)
* {card:Trader} — Triggers on when-gain instead of when-would-gain.

sections.heading: Cosmetic card changes
sections.body:
* {card:Bank}, {card:Charm}, {card:Coin of the Realm}, *{card:Contraband}*, {card:Counterfeit}, {card:Cursed Gold}, *{card:Diadem}*, {card:Fortune}, {card:Goat}, {card:Horn of Plenty}, {card:Idol}, *{card:Ill-Gotten Gains}*, *{card:Loan}*, {card:Lucky Coin}, {card:Magic Lamp}, {card:Philosopher's Stone}, {card:Relic}, {card:Scepter}, {card:Stockpile}, {card:Supplies}, {card:Treasure Trove}, *{card:Venture}* — Remove "when you play this" from Treasures. ({card:Spoils} still use the old wording but it is likely that it too will change in future reprint of Dark Ages.)
* {card:Bridge Troll}, *{card:Goons}*, {card:Groundskeeper}, {card:Haggler}, {card:Hoard}}, {card:Lighthouse}, *{card:Royal Seal}*, *{card:Talisman}*, {card:Tracker} — Rephrased "while this is in play" to "while you have this in play". (Later revised again in 2022 Errata.)
* *{card:Embargo}* — Rephrased "Trash this. If you did..." to "Trash this to", matching the 2016 Errata that was made for several other cards.
* {card:Noble Brigand} — Added a separating line to highlight the when-buy ability.
* {card:Peddler} — Rephrased for clarity.
* {card:Village Green} — Is revealed when played as a reaction.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: The **2023 Errata** changed cards giving extra turns to never allow more than two turns in a row.

sections.heading: Extra turn errata
sections.body: {card:Island Folk}, {card:Journey}, {card:Mission}, {card:Outpost}, {card:Possession}, and {card:Voyage} are changed to never allow more than two turns in a row. {card:Fleet} and {card:Seize the Day} however are not changed.

sections.heading: Cosmetic card changes
sections.body:
* {card:Baker}, {card:Young Witch} — "Setup:" is now written in bold text. ({card:Aqueduct}, {card:Arena}, {card:Basilica}, {card:Battlefield}, {card:Baths}, {card:Black Market}, {card:Colonnade}, {card:Defiled Shrine}, {card:Druid}, {card:Importer}, {card:Inherited}, {card:Labyrinth}, {card:Necromancer}, {card:Obelisk}, {card:Tax}, and {card:Way of the Mouse} have not been updated but are likely to to change in future reprints. *{card:Trade Route}* was removed before it could be printed with this change.)
* {card:Harem} — Renamed to {card:Farm} with new art.
* {card:Herald}, {card:Stonemason} — "Overpay:" is now written in bold text. (*{card:Doctor}* and *{card:Masterpiece}* were removed before they could be printed with this change.)
* {card:Elder} — Rephrased "choose one" to "choose" to not exclude cards like {card:Pawn} that normally give more than one choice.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body:
Since the initial release of Dominion in 2008, several official updates have been made, both to clarify the intention of rules and cards, and to tweak the game to make it better. The first errata were announced in 2016, and since 2019 there have been at least some updates every year.

The full list of all errata with explanations can be found on separate pages for each year:
2016,
2019,
2020,
2021,
2022,
2023,
2024,
2025,
2026

For a complete list of changes, see the Versions section on the page for each set or card.

Below is a summarized list of the functional changes that have been made to the rules and to each card. Note that rephrasings and other changes that don't affect how the card is played are omitted. If a card has had multiple errata, only the latest version is described here.

sections.heading: Rules
sections.body:
* Coffers — Can be spent at any time during your turn (2021).
* Debt — Can be paid off at any time during your turn (2024).
* Durations — No longer have any effect on future turns if the card has left play (2025).
** A Duration card played extra times by a Throne Room variant that has left play is only multiplied for the remainder of the turn it was played, not during future turns.
* Overpay — Overpay abilities take place when the bought card is gained, not before (2022).
* Playing cards — An effect that tries to play a card for the first time can only do so when the card is where the effect expects it to be (2021).
* Shuffling — When drawing more cards than available in your deck, first shuffle your discard and put it below the deck, then draw (2016).
* Stop-moving — An effect can move a card if it specifies where the card is coming from, or if the effect put the card where it is now. (2019).
** If a card isn't where the effect would expect it to be, or has moved away from there and then back, it can't move the card.
** Played cards expect to be in play; they can't move themselves if they aren't.
** Gained cards are expected to be where they were gained to, even if this isn't the discard pile.
** Cards in discard piles can be moved even if covered up by other cards; cards on top of a deck can't be moved once covered up.

sections.heading: Dominion
sections.body:
* {card:Cellar} — "**+1 Card**" instead of "draw" (2020 reverts 2016 errata).
* {card:Mine} — Trashing a card is optional (2016).
* {card:Moneylender} — Trashing a card is optional (2016).
* {card:Throne Room} — Playing a card is optional (2016).

sections.heading: Intrigue
sections.body: * {card:Masquerade} — Skip players with no cards in hand (2016).

sections.heading: Seaside
sections.body:
* *{card:Embargo}* — *(No dividing line.)* '{coin:+2}. Trash this to add an Embargo token to a Supply pile. (For the rest of the game, when a player buys a card from that pile, they gain a Curse.)' (2016, 2019)
* {card:Lighthouse} — *(No dividing line.)* **'+1 Action**. {coin:+1}. At the start of your next turn, {coin:+1}. Until then, when another player plays an Attack card, it doesn't affect you.' (2022)
* {card:Outpost} — 'You only draw 3 cards for your next hand. Take an extra turn after this one (but not a 3rd turn in a row).' (2016, 2023)
* *{card:Pirate Ship}* — The choice to produce {coin:+} is before the choice to attack (2016).
* {card:Treasury} — **'+1 Card**. **+1 Action**. {coin:+1}. (Dividing line) When you discard this from play, if you didn't gain any Victory cards in your Buy phase this turn, you may put this onto your deck.' (2022, 2026)

sections.heading: Alchemy
sections.body:
* {card:Alchemist} — *(No dividing line.)* **'+2 Cards**. **+1 Action**. At the start of Clean-up this turn, if you have a Potion in play, you may put this onto your deck.' (2022)
* {card:Herbalist} — *(No dividing line.)* **'+1 Buy**. {coin:+1}. Once this turn, when you discard a Treasure from play, you may put it onto your deck.' (2022)
* {card:Philosopher's Stone} — 'Count your deck and discard pile. {coin:+1} per 5 cards total between them (round down).' (2020)
* {card:Possession} — Cannot give a second turn in a row and the Possessing player also receives all {debt:} tokens (2016, 2023).

sections.heading: Prosperity
sections.body:
* {card:Bank} — '{coin:+1} per Treasure card you have in play (counting this).' (2020)
* {card:Hoard} — *(No dividing line.)* '{cost:2}. This turn, when you gain a Victory card, if you bought it, gain a Gold.' (2022, 2022)
* {card:Mint} — 'When you gain this, trash all non-Duration Treasures you have in play.' (2022, 2022)
* {card:Quarry} — *(No dividing line.)* Active this turn instead of while in play (2022).
* *{card:Trade Route}* — Trash a card before producing {coin:+} (2016).

sections.heading: Cornucopia & Guilds
sections.body:
* {card:Merchant Guild} — *(No dividing line.)* **'+1 Buy**. {coin:+1}. At the end of your Buy phase this turn, **+1 Coffers** per card you gained in it.' (2021)
* *{card:Princess}* — *(No dividing line.)* Active this turn instead of while in play (2022).
* {card:Soothsayer} — Each player both gains a Curse and draws a card before the next player does so (2016).

sections.heading: Hinterlands
sections.body:
* {card:Farmland} — 'When you gain this, trash a card from your hand and gain a non-Farmland card costing exactly {cost:2} more than it.' (2022)
* {card:Fool's Gold} — 'If this is the first time you played a Fool's Gold this turn, {coin:+1}, otherwise {coin:+4}.' (2020)
* {card:Haggler} — '{coin:+2}. This turn, when you gain a card, if you bought it, gain a cheaper non-Victory card.' (2022, 2022)
* {card:Highway} — *(No dividing line.)* Active this turn instead of while in play (2022).
* *{card:Oracle}* — "**+2 Cards**" instead of "draw" (2020 reverts 2016 errata).
* {card:Scheme} — **'+1 Card**. **+1 Action**. This turn, you may put one of your Action cards onto your deck when you discard it from play.' (2016)
* {card:Trader} — Triggers on when-gain instead of when-would-gain and exchanges the gained card for a Silver (2020).

sections.heading: Dark Ages
sections.body:
* {card:Band of Misfits} — [Action-Command] 'Play a non-Command non-Duration Action card from the Supply that costs less than this, leaving it there.' (2019, 2019, 2025)
* {card:Counterfeit} — Can only play non-Duration Treasures (2022).
* {card:Death Cart} — 'You may trash this or an Action card from your hand, for {coin:+5}' (2019)
* {card:Hermit} — *(No dividing line.)* 'Look through your discard pile. You may trash a non-Treasure from it or from your hand. Gain a card costing up to {cost:3}. At the end of your Buy phase this turn, if you didn't gain any cards in it, exchange this for a Madman.' (2022)
* {card:Hovel} — Can trash itself when a Victory card is gained instead of when bought (2022).
* {card:Pillage} — 'Trash this. If you did, gain 2 Spoils, and each other player with 5 or more cards in hand reveals their hand and discards a card that you choose.' (2019)
* {card:Procession} — Cannot play Duration cards (2019).
* {card:Storeroom} — "draw" instead of "**+1 Card**" (2016).

sections.heading: Adventures
sections.body:
* {card:Bonfire} — 'Trash up to 2 Coppers you have in play.' (2022)
* {card:Bridge Troll} — *(No dividing line.)* 'Each other player takes their –{cost:1} token. On this turn and your next turn, cards cost {cost:1} less. Now and at the start of your next turn: **+1 Buy**.' (2022)
* {card:Haunted Woods} — Triggers when gaining a card that was bought instead of buying (2022).
* {card:Inheritance} — 'Once per game: Set aside a non-Command non-Duration Action card from the Supply costing up to {cost:4}. Move your Estate token to it. (During your turns, Estates are also Command Actions with "Play the card with your Estate token, leaving it there.")' (2019, 2019, 2022, 2025)
* {card:Messenger} — Triggers when gaining a card in your Buy phase instead of when buying (2022).
* {card:Mission} — Cannot give a third turn in a row (2023).
* {card:Plan} — Triggers when gaining instead of when buying (2022).
* {card:Port} — Triggers when gaining instead of when buying (2022).
* {card:Storyteller} — **'+1 Action**. Play up to 3 Treasures from your hand. Then, **+1 Card**, and pay all of your {cost:} for **+1 Card** per {cost:1} you paid.' (2020, 2022)
* {card:Swamp Hag} — Triggers when gaining a card that was bought instead of buying (2022).

sections.heading: Empires
sections.body:
* {card:Basilica} — Triggers on gaining in your Buy phase instead of when buying (2022).
* {card:Chariot Race} — Draws (affected by the -1 card token) and reveals the card before the other player reveals (2025).
* {card:Charm} — Triggers on gaining instead of buying (2022).
* {card:Colonnade} — Triggers on gaining in your Buy phase instead of when buying (2022).
* {card:Defiled Shrine} — Triggers on gaining a Curse in your Buy phase instead of when buying (2022).
* {card:Donate} — Triggers at the start of your next turn (2022).
* {card:Encampment} — Returns to its pile, even if not in the Supply (2021).
* {card:Farmers' Market} — Add and remove token on its pile, even if not in the Supply (2021).
* {card:Forum} — Get +1 Buy when gained instead of when bought (2022).
* {card:Gladiator} — Trash a Gladiator from its pile even if it isn't in the Supply (2021).
* {card:Groundskeeper} — *(No dividing line.)* Active this turn instead of while in play (2022).
* {card:Mountain Pass} — Triggers immediately when the first Province is gained (2022).
* {card:Overlord} — [Action-Command] 'Play a non-Command non-Duration Action card from the Supply costing up to {cost:5}, leaving it there.' (2019, 2019, 2025)
* {card:Ritual} — Use the cost of the card after it was trashed instead of before (2025).
* {card:Rocks} — Gain the {card:Silver} directly to your deck or hand instead of moving it after gaining (2021).
* {card:Tax} — Triggers on gaining in your Buy phase instead of when buying (2022).
* {card:Temple} — Add and remove tokens on its pile, even if not in the Supply (2021).
* {card:Wild Hunt} — Add and remove tokens on its pile, even if not in the Supply (2021).

sections.heading: Nocturne
sections.body:
* {card:Crypt} — Cannot set aside Duration cards (2022).
* {card:Necromancer} — Turn the card face down before playing it (2020).
* {card:Tracker} — *(No dividing line.)* Active this turn instead of while in play (2022).

sections.heading: Renaissance
sections.body:
* {card:Citadel} — 'The first time you play an Action card during each of your turns, replay it afterwards.' (2022 reverts 2021 errata).
* {card:Experiment} — Returns to its pile, even if not in the Supply (2021).
* {card:Exploration} — Counts cards gained during the Buy phase instead of cards bought (2021, 2022).
* {card:Innovation} — 'Once during each of your turns, when you gain an Action card, you may play it.' (2022)
* {card:Lantern} — Affects {card:Border Guard|Border Guards} you play instead of those you own (2019).
* {card:Patron} — Reaction can only be used in Action phases (2021).
* {card:Scepter} — [Treasure-Command] Cannot replay Command cards (2024).

sections.heading: Menagerie
sections.body:
* {card:Gamble} — 'Discard the top card of your deck. If it's an Action or Treasure, you may play it.' (2025)
* {card:Reap} — The Gold no longer visits the discard pile (2025).
* {card:Way of the Mouse} — Cannot set aside a Duration card (2025).

sections.heading: Allies
sections.body:
* {card:Island Folk} — Cannot give a third turn in a row (2023).
* {card:Royal Galley} — Leave the played card in play until the next turn (2026).
* {card:Voyage} — Cannot give a third turn in a row (2023).

sections.heading: Plunder
sections.body: * {card:Journey} — 'You don't discard cards from play in Clean-up this turn. Take an extra turn after this one (but not a 3rd turn in a row).' (2023)

sections.heading: Promotional cards
sections.body:
* {card:Captain} — [Action-Duration-Command] Cannot play Command cards (2019).
* {card:Prince} — [Action-Duration-Command] 'You may set aside (on this) a non-Duration, non-Command Action card from your hand costing up to {cost:4}. At the start of each of your turns, play that card, leaving it set aside.' (2022)
* {card:Sauna} — *(No dividing line.)* Active this turn instead of while in play (2022).
* {card:Stash} — 'When shuffling this, you may look through your remaining deck, and may put this anywhere in the shuffled cards.' (2016)

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body:
The **2024 Errata** made few changes, mainly related to the release of Rising Sun.

The second edition of Cornucopia & Guilds was also released in 2024 but most updates to existing cards were already known from previous errata announcements.

sections.heading: Paying off Debt
sections.body:
Debt can now be paid off at any time during your turn, not just during a player's Buy phase.

This makes {card:Capital|Capital's} extra pay off during Cleanup redundant.

sections.heading: Function card changes
sections.body: * {card:Scepter} — Gained the Command type and no longer allows Command cards to be replayed, to avoid loops with {card:Enlightenment}.

sections.heading: Cosmetic card changes
sections.body:
* {card:Hunting Party} — Rephrased "reveal one" as "reveal a card".
* {card:Prince} — Text layout updated and added a missing comma.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: The 2021 Errata made some smaller changes to pre-Allies sets and consists mainly of cosmetic changes made for the 2021 re-printings of Alchemy, Adventures, Nocturne, and Renaissance. During 2021, there were also rule updates regarding when effects can play cards and when Coffers can be spent.

sections.heading: When effects can play cards
sections.body:
An effect that tries to play a card for the first time can only do so when the card is where the effect expects it to be.

This made the "if you do" part of {card:Reap} and "reveal it to" on {card:Village Green} redundant.

sections.heading: Spending Coffers
sections.body:
Coffers can now be spent at any time during your turn, not just at the beginning of the Buy phase.

To prevent additional Coffers from being gained during the Buy phase, the following cards are also updated:
* {card:Merchant Guild} — Now only gains Coffers at the end of the Buy phase.
* {card:Patron} — Now only triggers during the Action phase.

sections.heading: Functional card changes
sections.body:
* {card:Citadel} — Plays an Action twice instead of replaying it, meaning the Action is always played a second time if it was possible to play it the first time. (This was revised again in the 2022 Errata).
* {card:Donate}, {card:Mountain Pass} — Triggers at end of turn instead of between turns to avoid on-trash triggers in between turns. (This was revised again in the 2022 Errata).
* {card:Encampment}, {card:Experiment}, {card:Farmers' Market}, {card:Gladiator}, {card:Temple}, {card:Wild Hunt} — Refer to their piles, even if not in Supply. (This matters for things like {card:Ferryman}.)
* {card:Exploration} — Now only cares about cards bought during the most current buy phase.
* {card:Necromancer} — Now turns the chosen card face down before playing it to prevent loops.

sections.heading: Cosmetic card changes
sections.body:
* {card:Artificer} — Rephrased to include a comma.
* {card:Champion} — Rephrased "Attack card" to "Attack" and "Action" to "Action card".
* {card:Coin of the Realm}, {card:Royal Carriage} — Rephrased from "Directly after you finish playing an Action card" to "After you play an Action card".
* {card:Fool} — Change a comma to a colon.
* {card:Gladiator} — Rephrased "If they do not" to "If they don't".
* {card:Idol}, {card:Magic Lamp} — Clarified that they count themselves as in play.
* {card:Innovation} — Rephrased to no longer set the card aside before playing it.
* {card:Mill} — Rephrased "You may discard 2 cards, for {coin:+2}." to "You may discard 2 cards. If you do, {coin:+2}."
* {card:Opulent Castle} — Now reveals the discarded Victory cards.
* {card:Star Chart} — Rephrased "When you shuffle" to "When shuffling".
* {card:Teacher} — The clarifying parenthesis is no longer a separate sentence, reverting the previous change from the 2017 printing.
* {card:Treasure Hunter} — Rephrase "on their turn" to "in their turn".
* {card:Vineyard} — Changed "round down" to "rounded down", reverting the previous change from 2016.
* {card:Warrior} — Restored the original "For each Traveller" phrasing used before the 2017 printing.

sections.heading: Formatting changes
sections.body:
* Many cards got new text layout even though the text wasn't changed in the 2021 printings of Dominion, Intrigue, Alchemy, Adventures, Empires, and Nocturne.
* The background color in the text area became lighter for Reaction and Victory cards to improve text readability.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: The **2025 Errata** updated the rules for how Durations that leave play are handled to simplify tracking.

sections.heading: New rules
sections.body:
If a Duration card leaves play, it stops doing things on future turns. This also applies to Throne Room variants tracking repeated Durations.

Command variants such as {card:Band of Misfits} no longer stay in play for as long as the card they played would have stayed in play. These cards additionally got functional changes to no longer be able to play Duration cards anyway, so this change mainly applies to when a Command variant plays a Throne Room variant which plays a Duration. In this case, the second play of the Duration would not have any effect beyond the current turn.

sections.heading: Functional card changes
sections.body:
* {card:Band of Misfits}, {card:Inheritance}, {card:Overlord} — Can no longer play Duration cards.
* {card:Chariot Race} — Now draws the card first, which means it is affected by the -1 card token.
* {card:Gamble} — Discards the card without revealing it.
* {card:Reap} — The gained {card:Gold} no longer visits the discard pile.
* {card:Ritual} — Now uses the cost of the card after it was trashed instead of before.
* {card:Way of the Mouse} — Can no longer set aside a Duration card.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: A few individual cards were changed during 2026 without any official announcement being made.

sections.heading: Function card changes
sections.body:
* {card:Royal Galley} — Don't set the played card aside to avoid problems with the 2025 Duration rule change.
* {card:Treasury} — Triggers when discarded instead of at the end of the Buy phase (reverting the 2022 Errata).

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: **Dark Ages** is the seventh Dominion expansion. It was released in August, 2012. It is a large expansion. The box contains 35 sets of Kingdom cards, with 500 cards, as well as other new types of cards such as Shelters, Ruins, and {card:Spoils}. Many cards in Dark Ages have a theme related to trashing and upgrading.

sections.heading: Additional rules
sections.body:
* Dark Ages has two piles of cards that have a variety of cards in them: the Ruins pile has a mix of five different Ruins, and the {card:Knights} pile has ten different Knights. These piles should be shuffled before each game, as explained under Preparation. The only card that may be bought or gained or chosen from one of these piles is the card on top. Players cannot look through the piles, only at the top card; turn the top card over any time it is face down. If a card is returned to one of these piles with {card:Ambassador} (from Seaside), the returned card goes on top. Ruins cards with different names, and Knights with different names, count as differently named cards for cards that care about this. For example, if {card:Menagerie} (from Cornucopia) reveals a hand of {card:Copper}, {card:Ruined Market} and {card:Ruined Library}, then it will give +3 Cards. When {card:Contraband} (from Prosperity) is played, a player can name a Ruins or Knight, but that only stops that specific Ruins or Knight from being bought. However an {card:Embargo} token (from Seaside) placed on the Ruins or Knight pile will affect any cards bought from it.
* Players can buy Ruins even though they normally will not wish to. Ruins cards are Actions; they may be played in the Action phase, and count as Actions for things that refer to Action cards, such as {card:Procession}. The Ruins pile, when used, is in the Supply, and if it is empty that counts towards the normal end condition. Cards that try to get specific cards from the Supply fail to get a Ruins or Knight if the correct one is not the top one. For example, if you buy a {card:Ruined Market} with {card:Talisman} (from Prosperity), you only gain another Ruined Market if that is the top Ruins under the one you bought; if you use {card:Ambassador} (from Seaside) to return {card:Sir Martin} to the Supply, the next player will gain that Sir Martin, but the player after that will not gain a card, as the next Knight will not be Sir Martin.
* Many cards in Dark Ages do something "when you trash" that card. These abilities function no matter whose turn the card is trashed on. The player that a "when you trash this" ability functions for is the player told to trash the card, regardless of whose card trashed the card. These abilities happen directly after the card is put into the trash, and can function in the middle of resolving effects for an Action card; for example, if a player plays {card:Graverobber} and uses it to trash a {card:Cultist}, they first draw three cards for trashing Cultist, then continue with resolving Graverobber and gain a card costing up to {cost:8}. Cards can sometimes leave a player's deck without being trashed, such as by being returned to the Supply with Ambassador (from Seaside) or passed to another player with {card:Masquerade} (from Intrigue). When two or more cards are trashed at the same time, such as due to {card:Count}, first trash them all, then pick an order to resolve things that happen due to trashing them. A "when you trash" ability is not itself a way to trash a card; some other card will be needed to actually trash the card and make the ability happen.
* Six cards in Dark Ages are never part of the Supply: {card:Spoils}, {card:Madman}, {card:Mercenary}, and the three Shelters: {card:Hovel}, {card:Necropolis}, and {card:Overgrown Estate}. Keep these cards handy for when they are needed. These cards cannot be bought, and cannot be gained by cards that gain cards from the Supply, such as {card:Armory}. They cannot be returned to the Supply with Ambassador (from Seaside). They can end up in the trash if something trashes them. These piles being empty does not count towards the end condition for the game, or towards the count of empty piles for cards like {card:Poacher}.

sections.heading: Shelters
sections.body: *See the Shelters page.*

sections.heading: The original Lose Track rule
sections.body: *See the Lose Track rule page.*

sections.heading: The modified Lose Track rule, called Stop-Moving rule
sections.body: *See the Stop-Moving rule page.*

sections.heading: "No visiting" rule
sections.body:
* When a card is gained to a location other than a discard pile, it does not "visit" the discard pile – it goes directly to where it was gained. For example {card:Armory} gains cards directly to the top of a deck.
In conjunction with the Lose Track rule above, this means that when a card is gained somewhere other than the discard pile, a card that looks for a gained card will not lose track of it.

sections.heading: Recommended sets of 10
sections.body: See Recommended Kingdoms/Dark Ages.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body:
**Intrigue** is the first expansion to Dominion designed by Donald X. Vaccarino, released in 2009 by publisher Rio Grande Games. The box originally contained 25 sets of Kingdom cards. The first edition contained Basic Supply cards to support up to 4 players, or up to 6 players when combined with those from base Dominion.

The second edition of Intrigue was released in Fall 2016, updating wording and formatting on cards, removing the basic cards, and replacing 6 first-edition Kingdom cards with 7 new ones. The new cards are also available in an update pack provided to allow existing Intrigue sets to be updated to the second-edition form.

The second edition of Intrigue is also included in a newer English-language Big Box version.

sections.heading: Additional rules
sections.body:
*
Intrigue has cards that give players a choice between two or more options. A player given a choice picks any choice, even if unable to do the instruction, then does as much of it as they can.
For example, Sylvia plays {card:Steward} with one card left in her hand. She can pick the "trash 2 cards from your hand" option despite only having one card in hand. If she picks that option, she trashes the one card in her hand. Sometimes one of the options of a card with a choice is to make {coin:+}. To track the {cost:}, players can push the card up slightly from the line of played cards.

*
Intrigue has three Victory cards that have another type as well: {card:Farm}, {card:Mill}, and {card:Nobles}. These cards are both types for all purposes.
For example, since {card:Nobles} is an Action card, it can be played in the Action phase, can be trashed from the Supply with {card:Lurker}, and so on; since it is a Victory card, it is worth {vp:} when scoring, is put into a player's hand due to {card:Patrol}, and so on.

sections.heading: Recommended sets of 10
sections.body: See Recommended Kingdoms/Intrigue

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: **Alchemy** is the third expansion to Base Dominion by Donald X. Vaccarino, released in 2010 by publisher Rio Grande Games. The box contains 12 sets of Kingdom cards, and 1 basic card. The main themes of the set are {card:Potion|Potions} and Actions, featuring the only cards in the game with {potion} in their cost, and many cards encouraging decks filled with Action cards.

sections.heading: Preparation
sections.body:
* After you choose 10 Kingdom cards for the Supply, if any of them have {potion} in the cost, add the Potion pile to the Supply. Also add the Potion pile if you are using the promotional card {card:Black Market}, and the Black Market deck includes at least one card with {potion} in the cost. If you don't have any cards with {potion} in the cost in the Supply or in the Black Market deck, do not use the {card:Potion} pile in this game.
* When you have a {card:Potion} pile, put all 16 {card:Potion|Potions} in it, no matter how many players there are. In games using this pile, if the pile becomes empty, that will count towards the game ending condition, like any other Supply pile.

sections.heading: Potion
sections.body:
* Potion is a new Basic Treasure card. It costs {cost:4}, and when played produces {potion} rather than {cost:}. {potion} is a new resource, with no equivalent in {cost:}. You get a single {potion} per {card:Potion} played.
* To buy a card with {potion} in the cost, you need {potion}. For example to buy an {card:Alchemist}, which costs {cost:3}{potion}, you need both {cost:3} and {potion}. You could play a {card:Gold} and a {card:Potion}, then buy {card:Alchemist} with the {cost:3} and {potion} they produced. To buy two {card:Alchemist|Alchemists} in one turn, you need {cost:6} and two {potion} (and a +Buy). As with {cost:}, any unspent {potion} is lost at end of turn (but you will still have the {card:Potion} itself to replay for {potion} on future turns).
* Some cards refer to how much a card costs. Adding {potion} to a cost gives you a higher cost; {cost:3}{potion} is more than {cost:3}. More specifically:
** References to cards costing “up to” some cost only include {potion} if {potion} is in the given cost. If {potion} is in the cost, you can drop the {potion} and that is still "up to", but you cannot add {potion} if it is not there.
*** **Example:** {card:University} gains an Action card costing up to {cost:5}; it cannot gain a card with {potion} in the cost. However if you use {card:Remodel} to trash a card costing {cost:2}{potion}, you gain a card costing up to {cost:4}{potion}, which could be a card costing {cost:4}{potion}, {cost:4}, {cost:3}{potion}, {cost:3}, and on down to {cost:0}.
** Adding coins to a cost does not affect {potion} being in the cost or not. If {potion} was in the cost, it still is; if it was not, it still is not. Same with subtracting coins from a cost.
*** **Example:** {card:Remodel} allows you to gain a card costing up to {cost:2} more than the trashed card. Trashing a card that costs {cost:2} would not let you gain a card costing {cost:4}{potion} using {card:Remodel}. {card:Bridge} makes cards cost {cost:1} less this turn. This lowers the cost of a card costing {cost:4}{potion} to {cost:3}{potion}. It does nothing to the cost of a card costing just {potion}.
** References to cards costing some number of {cost:} “or more” include cards with or without {potion} in the cost.
*** **Example:** {card:Patrician} (from Dominion: Empires) checks to see if a card costs {cost:5} or more. {card:Apothecary} costs {cost:2}{potion} and so does not, since it doesn't have at least {cost:5} in its cost, but {card:Possession} costs {cost:6}{potion} and so does cost {cost:5} or more.
** References to a cost range in {cost:} does not include cards with {potion} in the cost.
*** **Example:** {card:Rogue} (from Dominion: Dark Ages) can trash a card costing from {cost:3} to {cost:6}. That means cards costing exactly {cost:3}, {cost:4}, {cost:5}, or {cost:6}. None of those have {potion} in the cost.
** Cards which look at the cost of a card in {cost:} do not do anything with {potion}.
*** **Example:** {card:Salvager} (from Dominion: Seaside) trashes a card, and produces +{cost:1} per {cost:1} the card cost. If you trash a card costing {cost:3}{potion}, you will just get +{cost:3}.
** Cards which check if two costs are the same include {potion} if it is there.
*** **Example:** {card:Swindler} (from Dominion: Intrigue) trashes a card, and has the player who lost it gain a card with the same cost. If {card:Swindler} trashes a card costing {cost:3}{potion}, that player will gain another card costing exactly {cost:3}{potion}.

sections.heading: Recommended sets of 10
sections.body: See Recommended Kingdoms/Alchemy

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body:
**Cornucopia** is the fifth Dominion expansion, released in June 2011. The basic theme of the set is cards that either create or reward variety in your deck and hand. It is a small expansion. The box contains 13 sets of Kingdom cards and is popular for its focus on engine-friendly cards. It is no longer sold as a separate item, instead being paired with Guilds in a standard box. It got paired also with Alchemy in other languages.

When the second edition of Cornucopia & Guilds was released, that replaced five Cornucopia Kingdom cards with five new ones.

sections.heading: Additional rules
sections.body:
* "In play" - Action cards and Treasure cards played face-up to a play area are in play until they are moved somewhere else—usually until they are discarded during a Clean-up phase. Only played cards are in play; set aside cards, trashed cards, cards in the Supply, and cards in hands, decks, and discard piles are not in play. Prizes that no-one has gained are not in play. Reaction abilities like {card:Horse Traders}' do not put those cards into play. Duration cards (from Dominion: Seaside), once played, remain in play until the turn they are discarded.
* A player may play his Treasure cards in any order and may choose not to play some (or even all) of the Treasure cards he has in his hand. During the Buy phase, a player must play all of the Treasures he wishes to play before he buys any cards, even if he has +Buys; he cannot play more Treasures after Buying a card.
* {card:Young Witch} adds an extra Kingdom card pile to the game. This extra pile is just like the other piles; if it is empty that counts for the game end condition, the cards in it can be bought and can be gained directly via cards like {card:Horn of Plenty}, etc. It is part of the Supply.
* There are five Prizes: {card:Bag of Gold}, {card:Diadem}, {card:Followers}, {card:Princess}, and {card:Trusty Steed}. These cards are never part of the Supply. That's the only new rule for Prizes, but it has various consequences. If the Prizes run out, that does not count towards the game end condition. The Prizes may not be bought, or gained via cards like {card:Horn of Plenty}; they may only be gained via the card {card:Tournament}, or via cards that gain cards other than from the Supply (such as {card:Thief} from Dominion). {card:Ambassador} (from Dominion: Seaside) cannot return Prizes to their pile. Trashed Prizes go to the trash pile, like other cards; they do not return to the Prize pile. When using {card:Black Market}, do not put Prizes in the Black Market deck. Prizes cannot be bought, but have a cost of {cost:0}, which matters for cards like {card:Remake}.
* A number of cards in Cornucopia care about cards being different. "Differently named" cards are simply cards with different names (like the Prizes) - they aren't copies of the same card. "Duplicate" cards are cards that have the same name - two copies of the same card.

sections.heading: Recommended sets of 10
sections.body: Note that the sets listed here are only the ones published before Cornucopia was combined with Guilds. For more recent recommended sets, see Cornucopia & Guilds Recommended sets of 10.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body:
**Hinterlands** is the sixth Dominion expansion, released in October 2011. The box contains 26 sets of Kingdom cards. The basic theme of the set is cards that either have or cause effects when you buy or gain them. Hinterlands offers a balance of engine, Big Money, and alternate VP cards. Since it was originally conceived as a standalone, Hinterlands was deliberately kept on the simpler side, but the "when you gain/buy" mechanic introduced makes the set compelling to novice and experienced players alike.

The second edition of Hinterlands was released in July 2022. It contains 9 new sets of Kingdom cards, which are also available on their own as an update pack, to allow existing Hinterlands sets to be updated to the second-edition form.

The 2011 release of Hinterlands is perceived to have pushed Dominion strategy away from heavily streamlined, small-deck Action engines and toward navigating bulky decks: it emphasizes sifting and Silver-gaining, and has no cards that enable you to thin your deck by more than one card at a time. Hinterlands also emphasizes diversity in Kingdom card types, being the only expansion whose Kingdom cards include multiple Treasures, Reactions, and Victory cards; in the second edition, Donald X. shifted the focus toward Reaction cards specifically, of which Hinterlands now has six.

sections.heading: When gained
sections.body:
* Many cards in Hinterlands do something "when you gain" that card or another card.
** You can gain a card by gaining it directly, such as with {card:Workshop}, or by buying it.
** "When you gain this" happens directly after you gain the card; the card will be in your discard pile already (or wherever else it was put) when you resolve that ability.
** When playing a card, its "when you gain" ability no longer does anything.
* Examples:
** You buy {card:Border Village}, you gain it. Its ability happens; you gain a cheaper card. You choose to gain {card:Souk}. Souk's "when you gain this" ability happens, and you may trash up to 2 cards from your hand.
** You play {card:Haggler}, then buy Border Village, gaining it. Its ability happens and you gain a {card:Duchy}. Haggler's ability also happens, and you choose to gain another Haggler for gaining the Border Village. Haggler doesn't give you another card for gaining the Duchy or the Haggler, since Haggler only cares about you gaining cards that you bought.
** You play Border Village. You get +1 Card and +2 Action. You do not gain a card; that only happens when you gain Border Village, not when you play it.

sections.heading: When discarded
sections.body:
* Hinterlands has three cards that can do something when discarded: {card:Trail}, {card:Tunnel}, and {card:Weaver}.
** You cannot simply choose to discard these cards; something has to let you or make you discard them, to activate those abilities. The key thing to look for is a card actually telling you to "discard" cards.
** These abilities can happen on your own turn (such as due to {card:Oasis}), or on someone else's (such as due to {card:Margrave}). They do not happen in Clean-up, when you normally discard all of your played and unplayed cards.
** These abilities work when the card is discarded from anywhere - for example, from your hand (such as due to {card:Oasis}) or from your deck (such as due to {card:Cartographer}), or from being in Exile (a Exile from Dominion: Menagerie).
** If the card would not necessarily be revealed (such as when discarding multiple cards to {card:Cartographer}), you have to reveal it to make the ability happen.
** These abilities are optional, even if the card was already revealed for some other reason.
** These abilities do not function if cards are put into your discard pile without being discarded, such as when you gain a card, or when your deck is put into your discard pile (such as with {card:Messenger} from Dominion: Adventures).
** These abilities only happen once per time the card is discarded - you can't discard one {card:Tunnel} and reveal it twice for two {card:Gold|Golds}.
** If you discard multiple cards at once (e.g. to {card:Margrave}), they are all discarded at once, and then the abilities happen one at a time. This means for example that if you discard two {card:Trail|Trails} to a Margrave, and playing the first Trail causes you to shuffle, you won't be able to reveal the second Trail (as it's lost in your deck at that point).

sections.heading: Additional first-edition rules
sections.body:
* Many cards in Hinterlands do something "when you gain" or "when you buy" that card or another card.
** When you buy a card, you first buy it, then gain it. So, for example, if you have {card:Haggler} in play and buy {card:Embassy}, you first resolve {card:Haggler|Haggler's} "when you buy" ability, then gain {card:Embassy}, then resolve {card:Embassy|Embassy's} "when you gain" ability.
** When you gain a card without buying it, "when you gain" abilities will still happen, but "when you buy" abilities will not.
** "When you gain this" happens directly after you gain the card; the card will be in your discard pile already (or wherever else it was put) when you resolve that ability.
** When playing a card, its "when you gain/buy" abilities no longer do anything.
** You can sometimes buy a card without gaining it, such as by using {card:Trader} to gain {card:Silver} instead. You can also sometimes gain cards when it is not your turn.
** The player that "when you buy" things happen for is the player who paid for the card, and the player that "when you gain" things happen for is the player who actually gained the card. Those are normally the same person, but can be different, for example due to the Dominion: Alchemy card {card:Possession}.
* Examples:
** You buy {card:Border Village}. You gain it. Its ability happens; you gain a cheaper card. You choose to gain {card:Cache}. {card:Cache|Cache's} "when you gain this" ability then happens, and you gain 2 {card:Copper|Coppers}.
** You buy {card:Farmland}. Its ability happens; you choose to trash an {card:Estate} from your hand and gain a {card:Noble Brigand}. {card:Noble Brigand} has a "when you buy this" ability, but you did not buy it, so that ability does not do anything. Then you gain the {card:Farmland}.
** You play {card:Border Village}. You get +1 Card and +2 Actions. You do not gain a card; that only happens when you gain {card:Border Village}, not when you play it.

sections.heading: Recommended sets of 10
sections.body: See Recommended Kingdoms/Hinterlands.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body:
**Guilds** is the eighth expansion of Dominion. It was released in June 2013. The box contains 13 sets of Kingdom cards. The set has two main themes—cards that give Coffers, and cards that you can overpay for, which are signified by a "+" in their cost. There are also two cards that name cards, several very wordy cards, and several cards whose art features bald people. It is no longer sold as a separate item, instead being paired with Cornucopia in a larger box.

Early printings of Guilds used the wording "take a Coin token" where the revised edition of the combined expansion Guilds & Cornucopia has +X Coffers as a vanilla bonus.

When the second edition of Cornucopia & Guilds was released, that replaced three Guilds Kingdom cards with three new ones.

sections.heading: Coffers
sections.body:
* Some cards in Guilds put tokens on a player's Coffers. "+1 Coffers" means "add a token to your Coffers mat." In a player's Buy Phase, before buying anything, that player may remove tokens from their Coffers for {coin:+1} each.
* Coin tokens are provided for this. They are not component-limited; players may use a substitute if they run out. The same tokens are provided in Dominion: Seaside and Dominion: Prosperity; they can all be mixed together.
* Coin tokens being used in other ways, such as on the {card:Pirate Ship} mat for Dominion: Seaside, cannot be removed for {coin:+1}; just the Coin tokens on a player's Coffers mat.
* Coin tokens come from the supply of Coin tokens, and return there; they are not taken from other mats or other players.
* Coin tokens can only be removed from a player's Coffers in that player's Buy Phase (or when instructed by a card such as {card:Butcher}); they cannot be used when buying a card via the promotional card {card:Black Market}.

sections.heading: Overpay
sections.body:
* Some cards can be "overpaid" for. The costs for these cards have a "+" next to the coin symbol. A player may pay any additional amount for such a card, and then gets an effect based on how much extra was paid.
* {card:Potion|Potions} (from Dominion: Alchemy) may be used in overpaid amounts if desired, although this is not always meaningful.
* Debt (from Dominion: Empires) cannot be overpaid.
* Players may choose not to overpay, even if they have extra coins, but cannot choose to overpay {cost:0}; to overpay, a player has to actually pay more than the cost.
* The coins used to overpay are gone after spending them to overpay; they cannot be then used to buy something else.
* Overpaying happens when a card is bought, which is before it is gained.
* Players can only overpay for a card when buying it, not when gaining it some other way.
* The "+" is just a reminder; a card with "+" in the cost still has its normal cost for all purposes. For example if a player plays {card:Haggler} (from Dominion: Hinterlands), then buys Masterpiece, overpaying, Haggler will still gain them a card costing less than {cost:3}, the cost of Masterpiece. Similarly, Masterpiece could be the Bane card for {card:Young Witch}, since it costs {cost:3}.
* Reducing the costs of cards via {card:Bridge} (from Dominion: Intrigue) does not interact with overpay; for example, if you play five Bridges and have {cost:5} total to spend, Herald would cost {cost:0}, but if you bought one the most you could overpay for it would still be {cost:5}.

sections.body: Note that the sets listed here are only the ones published before Guilds was combined with Cornucopia. For more recent recommended sets, see Cornucopia & Guilds Recommended sets of 10.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body:
:*This page is about a fundamental element of all games of Dominion. For the specific card with a similar name, see Supplies.*

The **Supply** consists of all the cards a player is able to buy in a game. These include the Kingdom cards, the basic Treasure and Victory cards, {card:Curse|Curses}, and Ruins if they are available. Some cards, such as Rewards, {card:Spoils}, and cards in the {card:Black Market} deck are not in the Supply, but are able to be gained or otherwise acquired through the effects of specific other cards.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body:
A normal game of Dominion has a Supply consisting of {card:Estate|Estates}, {card:Duchy|Duchies}, {card:Province|Provinces}, {card:Copper}, {card:Silver}, {card:Gold}, {card:Curse|Curses}, and 10 piles of Kingdom cards (which are usually, but not always, mostly Actions). Some expansions add to the Supply:
* Alchemy adds {card:Potion|Potions} when {potion}-costing cards are in the Kingdom.
* Prosperity can add {card:Colony|Colonies} and {card:Platinum}.
* Cornucopia & Guilds has {card:Young Witch} which adds an 11th Kingdom card as its Bane.
* Dark Ages add Ruins when any of the Looters are present.
* Rising Sun has {card:Approaching Army} which adds an 11th Kingdom card that must be an Attack.

Ordinarily each pile in the Supply consists of several copies of the same card. The three exceptions to this are Ruins, {card:Knights}, and Split piles, which are each Supply piles containing two or more differently named cards; in these cases, only the top card of the pile is visible to players and available to be bought or gained. For this reason, although the entirety of any Supply pile is physically part of the Supply, only the top card of any pile is considered to be "in the Supply". For instance, when {card:Band of Misfits} requires you to choose a "card in the Supply", you may not choose a card in the Ruins or Knights pile other than the one on top.

A player can always check how many cards are left in any Supply pile, as well as any non-Supply pile.
If three or more piles in the Supply are empty at the end of a turn, the game ends. The game end condition for 5-6 player games is four or more piles.

When you choose a card to buy or gain, unless otherwise instructed, you must choose a card in the Supply.

Anything that is not from a Basic card pile or a Kingdom card pile is not considered to be part of the Supply.

See non-Supply for information about cards that are not part of the Supply and a list such cards. These cards cannot be bought normally, only gained or played in specific ways.

The trash is not part of the Supply. While the cards in it can come originally from the Supply, you cannot normally buy or gain from the trash. However there are some cards that can gain cards from the trash. See trash gainer for a list of such cards.

There are also several "Card-shaped things" that aren't cards, for example Events and Artifacts. These can never become part of a player's deck and are not considered part of the Supply.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body:
**Dominion**, sometimes called **Base Dominion**, the **Base Set**, or simply **Base**, is the first Dominion game created by Donald X. Vaccarino. It was released in 2008 by publisher Rio Grande Games. The box originally contained 25 sets of Kingdom cards and basic Supply cards to support up to 4 players.

The second edition of the base set was released in Fall 2016, improving wording and formatting on cards, updating basic card artwork, replacing the Trash card with a mat, and replacing 6 obsolete first-edition Kingdom cards with 7 new ones. The new cards are also available in an Update Pack provided for players owning the first edition of Dominion.

The Base set is also included in both the English and German Big Boxes and other collections.
